fact: Dacono's code makes it unlawful for the occupant of any premises to own or harbor more than three dogs, three cats, or four dogs and cats combined, with a litter exempt until it is six months old.
quote: (a) It shall be unlawful for the occupant of any premises within the City to own or harbor more than a total of three (3) dogs, or three (3) cats, or a combination of dogs and cats not to exceed four (4) in number provided, however, when the premises is an approved feeding station under the City's TNR program, the feral cat colony shall not be counted toward the maximum number established in this Section during the period of time feeding is authorized by the TNR program. (b) When a dog or a cat has a litter, the prohibition set forth in this Section shall not apply until such time as the puppies or kittens are six (6) months of age.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 7-82, Maximum number (Ord. 420, 1992; Ord. 693, 2007; codified through Ord. No. 1011, March 9, 2026)

fact: Dacono's code makes it unlawful to breed, buy, sell or board dogs, or to train dogs for guard or sentry work, as a business or activity within the city.
quote: It is unlawful for any person, partnership or corporation to engage in the business or activity of breeding, buying, selling or boarding dogs or engage in the training of dogs for guard or sentry purposes, within the City.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 7-81, Kennels prohibited (Ord. 372, 1990)

fact: Dacono's zoning code defines a kennel as any premises where four or more animals older than four months are harbored.
quote: Kennel means any premises, building or structure in or on which four (4) or more animals of more than four (4) months of age are harbored.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 16-51, Kennel (definition)

fact: Dacono's code makes it unlawful for an owner to let animal feces stay on any public or private property and requires pickup into a trash receptacle immediately after the animal goes.
quote: It is unlawful for any owner to permit any animal feces to remain on any public or private property. Any such feces shall be picked up and disposed of in a trash receptacle by the owner or other person having charge of the animal immediately after the deposit of the feces by the animal.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 7-88, Failure to pick up and dispose of feces (Ord. 372, 1990)

fact: Dacono's code lets animals run loose on their owner's premises, counts a dog that leaves by its own efforts as running at large, and requires a leash no longer than six feet off the property.
quote: However, where the owner has made reasonable provision to confine the animal on the owner's premises and the animal leaves the premises due to the acts of third persons, the owner shall not be in violation of this Article. An animal which leaves its owner's premises due to its own efforts shall be deemed to be running at large; owners shall be responsible to foil their pets' attempts to run at large. … It is unlawful for any person owning, harboring or in charge of any dog to permit the dog to run at large unless the dog is restrained by a substantial leash not to exceed six (6) feet in length which is in the actual control of a person competent to restrain the dog. … The provisions of this Article shall not prohibit animals running at large on the premises of the owner or other person having charge of the animal.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Chapter 7, Article 4 (Animals): Sec. 7-60 definition of running at large, Sec. 7-74 and Sec. 7-77

fact: Anyone in Dacono who has kept a dog six months or older for four days must get a City dog license, paid annually, and every license expires April 30.
quote: Any person having had custody of any dog six (6) months of age or older for four (4) days shall procure a dog license. License fees shall be paid annually to the City Clerk. … All dog licenses issued hereunder shall expire at 12:00 a.m. on April 30 of the year of issuance and the full license fee shall be paid for any fraction of the licensing year.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 7-68, License required (Ord. 420, 1992)

fact: Dacono's code sends a dog seen running at large to impound at an animal-care facility, and an impounded animal not redeemed within five days is deemed abandoned.
quote: Any dog observed running at large shall be taken up by a police officer or an animal control officer and impounded at a facility specializing in animal care. … If the animal is not redeemed within five (5) days, it shall be deemed abandoned and may be disposed of by adoption, donation or destruction at the discretion of the animal shelter.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Secs. 7-78 and 7-79 (Ord. No. 964, 2024)

fact: Dacono's City Council adopted Ordinance 1016, which prohibits nonfunctional turf, artificial turf and invasive plant species, on second reading by a unanimous vote on May 11, 2026.
quote: Mayor Morehead moved to approve Ordinance 1016, Amending the Dacono Municipal Code to Prohibit Nonfunctional Turf, Artificial Turf, and Invasive Plant Species, on Second Reading. The vote was unanimous, with Mayor Morehead declaring the motion carried.
source_label: City of Dacono City Council minutes, May 11, 2026, item D (Ordinance 1016, second reading)
notes: The minutes PDF is a scan (read as images). Municode's online code is codified through Ord. No. 1011 (Supp. 35) as of 2026-09-25; its ordinance bank lists Ord. 1016 but the PDF was still 'being processed'. Recheck for codification and move the source to the codified sections once they post.

fact: Under Ordinance 1016, Dacono allows turf and artificial turf only in functional recreational use areas such as playgrounds, sports fields and picnic areas, and prohibits it elsewhere on multifamily properties of 12 or more units and on commercial, institutional, industrial and common-interest community property.
quote: (d) Turf areas. Turf areas may be installed as sod or seeded. Turf and artificial turf may be installed only within functional recreational use areas, including playgrounds, sports fields, picnic areas, and other spaces that are used regularly for civic, community, or recreational purposes. All turf and artificial turf located outside of these areas is considered nonfunctional and is prohibited on all multi-family residential properties containing twelve (12) or more dwelling units and on non-residential properties, including but not limited to commercial, institutional, industrial, and common interest community properties. Turf shall not be installed in areas that are impractical or difficult to maintain and irrigate. This includes parkways under five (5) feet in width, slopes of four to one (4:1) or greater, and narrow or oddly shaped areas.
source_label: Dacono Ordinance No. 1016, Section 4, amending Municipal Code Sec. 16-656(d) (adopted May 11, 2026; City Council packet, item GB-D)
notes: Dacono's text says 'twelve (12) or more' dwelling units; the staff memo in the same packet describes HB25-1113 as covering multifamily developments 'with more than 12 units'.

fact: Ordinance 1016 defines functional turf in Dacono's zoning chapter as turf used for athletic fields, playgrounds, dog parks or other areas where turf is needed for active recreation or another functional use, and nonfunctional turf as turf kept mainly for looks, such as in rights-of-way, medians, parking lots and decorative areas.
quote: Sec. 16-43.5 Functional turf. Functional turf means turf that is used for athletic fields, playgrounds, dog parks, or other areas where turf is necessary for active recreation or other functional use. For purposes of this Chapter 16, functional turf shall be interpreted consistent with state law definitions for functional and nonfunctional turf as set forth in C.R.S. § 37-99-102. … Sec. 16-61.5 Nonfunctional turf. Nonfunctional turf means turf installed or maintained for primarily aesthetic or ornamental purposes and does not serve a functional use, including but not limited to turf within street rights-of-way, medians, parking lots, transportation corridors, or decorative landscape areas.
source_label: Dacono Ordinance No. 1016, Section 2, adding Municipal Code Secs. 16-43.5 and 16-61.5 (adopted May 11, 2026; City Council packet, item GB-D)

fact: Ordinance 1016 says non-potable irrigation service in Dacono does not permit nonfunctional turf, synthetic turf still cannot meet the landscape article's requirements except where the article expressly permits it, and no subdivision approval authorizes nonfunctional turf.
quote: Authorization of non-potable irrigation systems, connections, or service under this Chapter 13 shall not be interpreted to permit or require the installation or irrigation of nonfunctional turf where such turf is prohibited by Chapter 16 of this Code. … (g) Except where expressly permitted by this Article, artificial plants and synthetic turfs may not be used to meet the requirements of this Article. … No subdivision approval shall be deemed to authorize nonfunctional turf where the same is prohibited by Chapter 16, Article 28 of this Code.
source_label: Dacono Ordinance No. 1016, Sections 1, 5 and 6, amending Municipal Code Secs. 13-13, 16-657(g) and 17-250(b) (adopted May 11, 2026; City Council packet, item GB-D)
notes: The amended 16-657(g) adds 'Except where expressly permitted by this Article' to the 2014 wording that the shared record dacono-code-16-657g-not-landscaping quotes from Municode (not yet updated there).

fact: Dacono's planning staff wrote that Ordinance 1016 leaves regulating turf on property types outside the state's applicable-property list until that state requirement takes effect on January 1, 2028.
quote: The ordinance does not include regulations addressing the HB1113 requirement to regulate irrigation water use on property types not presently classified as applicable property, as that provision does not take effect until January 1, 2028. Deferring those regulations will allow the City and Council additional time to evaluate and formulate an appropriate approach for currently unaffected property classes.
source_label: City of Dacono Planning staff memo to City Council on Ordinance 1016, May 11, 2026 (City Council packet, item GB-D)

fact: Dacono's landscape design standards apply to new development, planned unit developments and a residential subdivision's streetscapes, open space, parks and HOA property, but not to single-family detached homes or to multifamily properties of four or fewer units outside their common areas.
quote: (a) These landscaping standards (and landscape plan review) shall apply to all public and private land located within the City, and shall apply to: (1) All new development and redevelopment of buildings and land, including applications for property of any size in commercial and industrial zone districts; (2) All planned unit development (PUD) applications; and (3) Residential subdivisions (streetscapes, hardscapes, open space, parks, homeowner association property). (b) Exemptions. These standards do not apply to the following land uses: (1) Single-family detached and multi-family residential properties of four (4) or fewer units not including common areas.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 16-651, Application (Ord. No. 787, 2014; codified through Ord. No. 1011, March 9, 2026)

fact: Dacono requires at least 20% of a development site to be landscaped with at least 75% living material within three years, 10% of any parking lot of 10 or more spaces, and a 50-foot landscape setback along I-25 and State Highway 52 with a tree for every 25 feet of frontage.
quote: (a) Minimum percent of landscaped area. The total landscaped area of all proposed development parcels shall comprise a minimum of twenty percent (20%) of the total site area within the property lines. … Landscaped area must include a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) living material based on mature plant sizes within three (3) years of planting. … (1) The minimum landscape setback along the existing I-25 and State Highway 52 corridors, and their associated frontage roads, shall be fifty (50) feet. That portion of a lot in any zone district which abuts the I-25 or State Highway 52 right-of-way shall be landscaped with a minimum of one (1) shade tree, or one (1) evergreen tree, for every twenty-five (25) linear feet of street frontage. … (2) For all parking lots consisting of ten (10) or more spaces, a minimum of ten percent (10%) of the total area designated as parking must be landscaped.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 16-662(a), (b)(1) and (c)(2), Site category requirements (Ord. No. 787, 2014)

fact: Dacono's landscape article holds high-water-use zones to 35% of a property's landscaped area and says turf grass should not exceed 25% of it, with exceptions possible for sports fields and high-traffic areas.
quote: (c) The total amount of high water use zones on a property shall not exceed thirty-five percent (35%) of the total landscaped area. (d) … The total area of turf should not exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of the total landscaped area. Exceptions may be allowed for uses such as sport fields and high traffic areas.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 16-656(c) and (d), Water-efficient landscape design (Ord. No. 787, 2014; both sentences kept by Ord. No. 1016, 2026)

fact: Dacono requires new multifamily developments of at least 10 units to include one recreational amenity, 100 units two and 200 units three, chosen from a list that includes two tot lots, a sport court, two picnic areas with grills and fenced off-leash pet areas.
quote: Recreational amenities. Multifamily developments that contain at least ten (10) units shall incorporate a minimum of one (1) of the following recreational amenities for its residents. Multifamily developments that contain at least one hundred (100) units shall incorporate at least two (2) recreational amenities. Multifamily developments that contain at least two hundred (200) units shall incorporate at least three (3) recreational amenities. a. Swimming pool. b. Clubhouse. c. Two (2) tot lots. d. Sport court. e. Two (2) picnic areas with grills. f. Fenced off-leash pet areas. g. Other recreational amenity, at the Community Development Director's discretion.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 16-813(j)(1), Multifamily design standards (Ord. No. 963, 2024)

fact: Since 2024 a new residential subdivision in Dacono must dedicate at least 10 acres of park land, open space and trails per 1,000 residents, generally 2.5 acres of pocket parks, 5 of neighborhood parks and 2.5 of open space and trails, or pay cash in lieu.
quote: (b) Applicability. Any person applying for approval of a preliminary, final, or minor subdivision plat for development of any area zoned and to be used for residential purposes within the City shall, as a condition of approval of the subdivision: (1) dedicate park land, open space and trails, and construct such park and recreation capital facilities on such park land and trails as required by this Article; or (2) pay the cash in lieu of dedication pursuant to Section 17-256. … (1) The amount of land dedicated for parks, open space and trails shall not be less than ten (10) acres of combined park land, open space, and trails per one thousand (1,000) residents of the development. … (2) The distribution of the required park land shall generally be as follows: a. Pocket parks: 2.5 acres/1,000 residents b. Neighborhood parks: 5 acres/1,000 residents c. Open space and trails: 2.5 acres/1000 residents (Ord. No. 967, §1, 2024)
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 17-251(b) and (c), Parks, open space and trails (Ord. No. 967, 2024)

fact: Dacono's code says pocket parks of a quarter acre to two acres may include play equipment and neighborhood parks of at least seven acres may include playground equipment, both held by an HOA or metro district, with the developer improving the pocket parks it dedicates.
quote: Pocket parks and trails required to be dedicated pursuant to this Article shall be improved by the applicant, subdivider, or owner in accordance with plans meeting the requirements of this Article. … (1) Pocket parks. Pocket parks provide opportunities for passive outdoor recreation at a sub-neighborhood scale. Pocket parks shall be located within one-quarter (¼) mile of the residences they are intended to serve and may include lawn areas, picnic shelters and tables, play equipment, artwork, or other amenities … Pocket parks shall be: a. One-quarter (¼) acre to two (2) acres in size; … e. Owned and maintained by an HOA or metropolitan district; … (2) Neighborhood parks. … Neighborhood parks may include multi-use lawn areas, picnic areas, playground equipment, small court games, community gardens, and playing fields and facilities as appropriate. Neighborhood parks shall be: a. Not less than a minimum size of seven (7) acres, unless the City Council approves a lesser amount; … e. Owned by the HOA or a metropolitan district. … The preliminary plat application shall include a master design plan for the pocket and neighborhood parks which shall include all of the park's amenities.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Secs. 17-252 and 17-253, Parks, open space and trails (Ord. No. 967, 2024)

fact: Dacono's R-2 zone lists day care centers among its permitted principal uses; the R-1 list of permitted principal uses carries a rule that day care operators certify their state license to the City Clerk for a local permit that renews with it; and R-1 allows nursery schools as an accessory use.
quote: Permitted principal uses in the R-1 district shall be as follows: … (4) Operators of day care centers shall certify to the City Clerk that they are duly licensed with the State, and the Clerk shall issue a local permit with the renewal date corresponding to that of the state license; … Accessory buildings and permitted accessory uses in the R-1 district shall be as follows: … (4) Nursery schools operated in compliance with applicable statutes and regulations thereunder. … Permitted principal uses in the R-2 district shall be as follows: … (10) Day care centers;
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Secs. 16-100(4) and 16-109(4) (R-1 district) and 16-130(10) (R-2 district)

fact: Dacono's City Parks page says pocket parks are in most neighborhoods, calls the splash park at Clem Dufour Park the biggest hit, and lists 15 nearby golf courses, Bella Rosa and Saddleback among them.
quote: While pocket parks are located in most neighborhoods, the biggest hit has been the Splash Park at Clem Dufor Park. Dacono is also close to the Carbon Valley Recreation Center. There are 15 nearby golf courses including the following and others: Bella Rosa … Saddleback
source_label: City of Dacono, City Parks page ('From Pocket Parks to Golf Courses')
notes: The City's page spells the park 'Clem Dufor'; its other pages spell it Dufour or DuFour.

fact: Bella Rosa Golf Course in Frederick is a 9-hole regulation course with a driving range, a putting green and a chipping area.
quote: Bella Rosa Golf Course is a meticulously designed 9-hole regulation course. … Each hole presents a unique challenge and an opportunity for you to sharpen your skills at our driving range, putting green, and chipping area. … 9-Hole Regulation Golf Course in Frederick, CO
source_label: Bella Rosa Golf Course, home page

fact: Saddleback Golf Club gives its address as Frontier Street in Firestone.
quote: 8631 Frontier Street Firestone, CO 80504
source_label: Saddleback Golf Club, home page (contact block)

fact: Dacono lies within two school districts, St. Vrain Valley and Weld County RE-8.
quote: Dacono is located within two different school districts, the St. Vrain Valley School District and the Weld County RE-8 School District.
source_label: City of Dacono, Education page

fact: Under its December 8, 2025 agreement with the Carbon Valley Parks and Recreation District, Dacono mows, waters and fertilizes its park fields and maintains park fences, irrigation, lighting and playground equipment, relies on the District for recreation programming and scheduling, keeps first priority for its parks with its own dates set by November 30 and May 31, and bars the District from renting or reserving the Clem DuFour splash pad.
quote: The City acknowledges the expertise of the District in the areas of recreation programming, scheduling and management, as well as athletic infield maintenance … Field Maintenance. The City shall provide for general field maintenance for the Parks, to include mowing, watering, fertilization, and provision of necessary utilities. … The City is responsible for maintaining capital assets of Parks, such as fences, gates, buildings, structures, irrigation systems, lighting, playground equipment, restroom facilities (not including port-a-lets placed by the District in accordance with this Agreement), and parking lots. … The City has first priority for the use and scheduling of City parks and other facilities. The City shall determine its dates of use on or before November 30th and May 31st of each year during the term of this Agreement for the six-month period of January-June and July-December, respectively. … Because the City prohibits renting or reserving the Splash Pad at Clem DuFour Park, the District will not be allowed to rent or reserve that amenity.
source_label: City of Dacono Resolution 25-74 and Intergovernmental Agreement with the Carbon Valley Parks and Recreation District, adopted December 8, 2025 (Secs. 1.3, 5.2 and 5.8)

fact: Dacono's draft 2026 Water Efficiency Plan says every HOA and park already has a dedicated outdoor meter and proposes ranking HOAs by water applied per acre, taking outreach first to the heaviest users in the second year.
quote: All HOAs and parks have dedicated outdoor meters. … In Year 1, Public Works staff should pull dedicated outdoor meter data for all existing HOAs and calculate a per-acre application rate for each. HOAs with the highest per-acre use should be prioritized for outreach in Year 2.
source_label: City of Dacono, 2026 Water Efficiency Plan (prepared by Spheros Environmental, dated July 15, 2026; posted for 60-day public comment), Tables 6 and 11
notes: A draft out for public comment on the City's Water Conservation page; recheck whether Council adopted it and whether the wording changed.

fact: Dacono's draft 2026 Water Efficiency Plan puts residential customers at about 80% of the City's water demand and commercial at roughly 17%, says the 15 largest users take about 11%, and finds outdoor use is about half of each year's demand.
quote: Residential customers account for the largest share of demand – about 80% each year. Commercial customers use roughly 17%, and Municipal uses make up the remaining 3%. … Indoor demand stays fairly constant, at about 4% of annual demand each month. … Over the course of a year, indoor and outdoor use each make up about half of total demand, but outdoor irrigation drives most of the summer peak. … Figure 8 summarizes water use among Dacono’s top 15 users (a mix of homes, businesses, and HOAs) who together account for about 11% of the City’s total annual demand.
source_label: City of Dacono, 2026 Water Efficiency Plan (dated July 15, 2026; draft for public comment), Sections 3.2.2, 3.2.4 and 3.2.5

fact: Dacono's draft 2026 Water Efficiency Plan lists six residential subdivisions on City water, estimating Sweetgrass at about 1,000 units and Sharpe Farms at about 850, both zoned R-1, with Legacy Park, about 300 units zoned R-2, building since 2020.
quote: The City currently serves six residential subdivisions (Sharpe Farms, Sweetgrass, Legacy Park, Eagle Meadow, Old Town/Glens, and Autumn Valley Ranch) … Table 2. Dacono Subdivisions (Subdivision Name · Zone District · Estimated # Units · Year Built): Sharpe Farms · R1 Residential · 850 · 2003-Present; Sweetgrass · R1 Residential · 1,000 · 2004-Present; Legacy Park · R2 Residential · 300 · 2020-Present; Eagle Meadow · RR-1 Rural Residential · 100 · 1990-2005; Old Town and the Glens · R-1 Residential and Manufactured Homes · 300 · 1970-1985; Autumn Valley Ranch · R-1 Residential and Manufactured Homes · 200 · 1990-2010 … Most customers are residential (Figure 3), with most accounts located within the six residential subdivisions identified in Table 2.
source_label: City of Dacono, 2026 Water Efficiency Plan (dated July 15, 2026; draft for public comment), Section 2.1.1 and Table 2
notes: Table 2 gives estimated units, not a lot count, and the plan ranks nothing. The statewide parcel file (Colorado Public Parcels, queried 2026-09-25) names about 800 residential parcels Glens of Dacono and about 550 Sweetgrass, so the two sources order the subdivisions differently: no page calls one of them the largest.

fact: Dacono's Planning Area adds about 22 square miles of largely undeveloped land between State Highway 52, Weld County Roads 21 and 6 and I-25, and the City's water plan expects service to grow toward about 70,000 residents.
quote: Beyond its current boundaries, Dacono’s Planning Area includes another 22 square miles (about 14,000 acres) of largely undeveloped land, generally bounded by State Highway 52 to the north, Weld County Road 21 to the east, Weld County Road 6 to the south, and Interstate 25 to the west. As this area develops, the City’s water service area is expected to expand significantly, eventually serving a population of about 70,000 residents. … Commercial and industrial customers make up a smaller share of accounts and are concentrated mainly along the Interstate 25 and State Highway 52 corridors (Figure 1). Based on publicly available county assessor data, Dacono currently serves about 360 acres of commercial and industrial development.
source_label: City of Dacono, 2026 Water Efficiency Plan (dated July 15, 2026; draft for public comment), Section 2.1.1

fact: Dacono's draft 2026 Water Efficiency Plan judged further landscape ordinances to have limited potential for added savings for now, given the City's 2026 landscape code and the state's turf laws, and did not make them a priority.
quote: Given the City’s existing WaterWise Landscape Code and this new state legislation, additional landscape-focused ordinances were judged to have limited potential for meaningful additional savings right now, so they weren’t identified as a priority.
source_label: City of Dacono, 2026 Water Efficiency Plan (dated July 15, 2026; draft for public comment), Chapter 5

fact: Dacono's code bars licensing a dog without proof of rabies vaccination.
quote: No dog shall be licensed without proof of rabies vaccination as provided in this Article.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 7-70, License - proof of vaccination required (Ord. 420, 1992)

fact: Dacono's code makes it unlawful to keep an animal that disturbs the peace and comfort of the neighborhood.
quote: It is unlawful for any animal owner or keeper to harbor, maintain or permit on any premises under his or her control any animal which disturbs the peace and comfort of the inhabitants of the neighborhood or interferes with any person in the reasonable and comfortable enjoyment of life and property.
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 7-75, Animal disturbing peace prohibited (Ord. 372, 1990)

fact: The Dacono Police Department's Animal Control page says dogs must be leashed off the owner's property except in a designated off-leash area, that waste pickup applies both on and off the owner's property, and that owners must keep a dog from biting, chasing, threatening, barking or howling at anyone.
quote: Dogs must be on a leash when off the owner’s property except when walking in a designated off-leash area Dog owners must pick up and properly dispose of their dog’s defecation both on and off the owner’s property A dog owner must ensure their dog does not bite, injure, chase, threaten, bark, howl at, or disturb anyone
source_label: City of Dacono Police Department, Animal Control page

fact: The splash pad at Clem Dufour Park is open from Memorial Day to Labor Day and is not available for rental.
quote: The splash pad is open seasonally from Memorial Day to Labor Day, 9 am to 8 pm daily. Please note that the splash pad at Clem Dufour Park is not available for rental.
source_label: City of Dacono, Splash Pad page (Clem Dufour Park)

fact: Dacono's R-2 district lists one-, two- and three-family dwellings and multifamily dwellings among its permitted principal uses.
quote: Permitted principal uses in the R-2 district shall be as follows: (1) One (1) family dwelling; (2) Two (2) family dwelling; (3) Three (3) family dwelling; (4) Multifamily dwelling;
source_label: Dacono Municipal Code Sec. 16-130, R-2 district permitted principal uses (codified through Ord. No. 1011, March 9, 2026)
